description: What `rig fork assess` looks for in a repository before it is forked, and what each finding asks of the person forking. The assessment reads one revision of a git clone and nothing else (no network, no clock), so the same clone at the same revision always gives the same report. See docs/forks.md.

obligations: No conditions, but credit upstream anyway: the history is the record of who wrote it.

history.shallow.responsibility: Fetch the full history (git fetch --unshallow) and assess again: authorship and licence history are what you inherit.

licence.missing.responsibility: Without a licence the code is all rights reserved. You may read it, but not copy, change or publish it. Ask the copyright holders for a licence, or do not fork.

licence.unrecognised.responsibility: Read the licence yourself before forking. If it permits forking, add its fingerprint and obligations to config/fork-assessment.json so the next assessment classifies it.

licence.terms.responsibility: These conditions travel with every copy you publish. A deleted or archived upstream changes none of them: a licence once granted is not withdrawn.

licence.copyright.responsibility: These holders keep their copyright. Keep these lines exactly; add yours beside them only for what you write.

notice.carry.responsibility: Carry the NOTICE file unchanged in every distribution, packages included. You may append your own attribution to it.

third-party.licences.responsibility: These files are under another licence than the project's. Keep their headers, ship that licence's text, and list them in a THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES file.

third-party.vendored.responsibility: Vendored code keeps its own licence and authors. Check each directory's licence and record it in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES before publishing.

names.packages.responsibility: Upstream publishes under these names. Never publish under them, never claim to be their continuation, and pick a name no one would mistake for upstream's.

names.brand-assets.responsibility: Logos and icons identify upstream's brand, which the code licence does not grant. Replace them before you publish anything.

names.trademark.responsibility: Upstream states a trademark policy. Read it and follow it when you name, describe and brand the fork.

contribution.ai-policy.responsibility: Upstream states a policy on AI or LLM use. Follow it in everything you send upstream, or send nothing; if the fork is AI-assisted, say so in its README.

contribution.cla.responsibility: Upstream asks contributors to sign a CLA. Anything you offer back needs it, and code from your fork's own contributors may not be offerable unless they sign too.

contribution.dco.responsibility: Upstream signs off commits (DCO). Keep signing off if you mean to offer changes back.

people.single-maintainer.responsibility: One person wrote most of this. If they stop, your fork may become what users depend on: budget for owning it, and credit them prominently.

people.recent-single-maintainer.responsibility: Recent work rests on one person. Expect upstream to stop or change direction without notice; keep your own copy of every ref you depend on.

people.personal-data.responsibility: The history holds contributors' names and email addresses. Keep the history as provenance, but do not republish or reuse contributor data beyond it.

activity.ended.responsibility: Upstream says it is ended or deprecated. Present the fork as a fork, never as the official successor, and be explicit about how much maintenance you commit to.

activity.stale.responsibility: Nobody has committed for a long time. Look for an announcement, a successor or a living fork before starting another, and expect to carry security fixes and support yourself. Present the fork as a fork, never as the successor.

history.unmerged-refs.responsibility: These refs hold work that is not on the assessed revision. Push them to your fork now if you may need them: they disappear with upstream.

ownership.concentration.responsibility: This is whose code you are carrying. Your fork's README, package metadata and release notes should credit them in proportion.
